items.title: “EVERYTHING”: The Black Skirts’ album ending and Japanese introduction
items.description: Announced as a closing track in 2016, “EVERYTHING” took its place on TEAM BABY before Jo Hyu-il chose it for his Japanese debut.
items.altText: “EVERYTHING”: The Black Skirts’ album ending and Japanese introduction — indiek. Original typographic article card.

items.title: Sharing the work: one circle in Korean shoegaze
items.description: Five years after Downfall of the Neon Youth, credits and concert accounts trace shared production, guest vocals and organising—with a connection to Brazil.
items.altText: Sharing the work: one circle in Korean shoegaze — indiek. Original typographic article card.

items.title: What spring means in HANRORO’s “Let Me Love My Youth”
items.description: Her debut’s dedication and a later concert theme connect personal flowering with other people’s beginnings.
items.altText: What spring means in HANRORO’s “Let Me Love My Youth” — indiek. Original typographic article card.

items.title: The private worlds of youra
items.description: From “Flicker” to “MIMI” and “Motif”, three songs follow youra’s personal writing through a changing circle of collaborators.
items.altText: The private worlds of youra — indiek. Original typographic article card.

items.title: Inside sunwoojunga’s “Run with Me”
items.description: A trip taken alone became an offer to go together. The story behind “도망가자”, and the expectations that followed it onto the stage.
items.altText: Inside sunwoojunga’s “Run with Me” — indiek. Original typographic article card.

items.title: Where to go after Yerin Baek’s “0310”
items.description: The writing process behind tellusboutyourself offers a route from “0310” to her next album.
items.altText: Where to go after Yerin Baek’s “0310” — indiek. Original typographic article card.

items.title: The Black Skirts — EVERYTHING
items.description: “EVERYTHING” is a love song from TEAM BABY. It first came out as a single in 2016, a year before the album.
items.altText: indiek listening notes: The Black Skirts — EVERYTHING. Typographic card.

items.title: sunwoojunga — Run with Me
items.description: Here’s “Run with Me” at sunwoojunga’s SERENADE concert, shared on her own channel. The song comes from her 2019 album Serenade; this performance was recorded at Sogang University’s Mary Hall.
items.altText: indiek listening notes: sunwoojunga — Run with Me. Typographic card.

items.title: Car, the garden — Tree
items.description: Here’s Car, the garden singing “Tree” for Begin Again’s Open Mic series. The song first came out as a single in April 2019.
items.altText: indiek listening notes: Car, the garden — Tree. Typographic card.

items.title: Choi Yu Ree — Forest
items.description: “Forest” is about feeling small among other people, and finding a place with them. Choi Yu Ree wrote it for her 2022 single release Stroll. This version is from a Bugs-ker live session.
items.altText: indiek listening notes: Choi Yu Ree — Forest. Typographic card.

items.title: BOL4 — Eternal love
items.description: Ahn Ji-young sings “Eternal love” (사랑할 수밖에) at BOL4’s 2024 Bloom concert in this clip from her own channel. The song is from the 2023 EP Merry Go Round.
items.altText: indiek listening notes: BOL4 — Eternal love. Typographic card.

items.title: ESEGYE — RomanceYouthLove
items.description: “RomanceYouthLove” was one of ESEGYE’s first releases. This recording is from their first BLIND concert at Veloso Hongdae, shared by the band themselves.
items.altText: indiek listening notes: ESEGYE — RomanceYouthLove. Typographic card.

items.title: SE SO NEON — The Wave
items.description: “The Wave” keeps going after the last vocal line, with an extended instrumental ending. This version comes from the 2020/NEON concert, filmed at YES24 Live Hall on December 7, 2019.
items.altText: indiek listening notes: SE SO NEON — The Wave. Typographic card.

items.title: YdBB — ONCE
items.description: “ONCE” is about letting someone go while hoping they’ll remember you kindly. Yu Dabin describes that farewell in the band’s release interview for the October 2023 single.
items.altText: indiek listening notes: YdBB — ONCE. Typographic card.

items.title: WhiteUsedSocks — Don’t feel sad
items.description: “Don’t feel sad” comes from WhiteUsedSocks’ early days. Jung Jaeheon wrote and composed the song, released in June 2017, before The Little Match Boy and Through Yearning.
items.altText: indiek listening notes: WhiteUsedSocks — Don’t feel sad. Typographic card.

items.title: Motte — Don’t run away
items.description: “Don’t run away” was part of the September 2018 soundtrack to A-TEEN. It’s an easy place to meet Motte’s music, even if you’ve never seen the series.
items.altText: indiek listening notes: Motte — Don’t run away. Typographic card.

items.title: HANRORO — Even if you leave
items.description: “Even if you leave” is about the things that are hard to let go of, and the habit of blaming yourself after they’re gone. HANRORO wrote both the words and music.
items.altText: indiek listening notes: HANRORO — Even if you leave. Typographic card.

items.title: Kim Sawol — Someone
items.description: “Someone” holds affection and doubt together. It’s from Kim Sawol’s second album, Romance, released in September 2018.
items.altText: indiek listening notes: Kim Sawol — Someone. Typographic card.

items.title: Yerin Baek — 0310
items.description: “0310” is sung in English, with the words on screen in Baek’s own lyric video. It’s from her 2019 album Every letter I sent you.
items.altText: indiek listening notes: Yerin Baek — 0310. Typographic card.

items.title: gongwon — Flower
items.description: The speaker in “Flower” hoped to bloom, but compares themselves to mold in a damp room. The song pairs that harsh self-image with a wish to keep growing and be loved. This is the official recording from gongwon’s EP 0.
items.altText: indiek listening notes: gongwon — Flower. Typographic card.

items.title: Yebit — Only You
items.description: In “Only You”, a walk through Seoul Forest brings a changed relationship into focus. The speaker still wants comfort from the person they struggle to face. Yebit sings it here at the Rolling 31st anniversary concert.
items.altText: indiek listening notes: Yebit — Only You. Typographic card.

items.title: Baek A — Amor
items.description: A love remembered as a film, a sky full of stars, and a moment still taking shape. Baek A sings “Amor” (첫사랑) here for MONTBEST LIVE. A poetic English adaptation follows below.
items.altText: indiek listening notes: Baek A — Amor. Typographic card.

items.title: youra — MIMI
items.description: “MIMI” calls to someone who has disappeared. youra wrote the lyrics and composed the song with Cosmic Boy for GAUSSIAN. The recording here is the ONSTAGE × D Museum live performance.
items.altText: indiek listening notes: youra — MIMI. Typographic card.

items.title: Sondia — Grown Ups
items.description: “Grown Ups” follows someone worn down by the day, wondering whether their small world will ever smile back. Sondia recorded it for the 2018 drama My Mister. This official OST music video uses scenes from the series.
items.altText: indiek listening notes: Sondia — Grown Ups. Typographic card.

items.title: moneto — She (Feat. MRCH)
items.description: “She” asks that someone’s memories stay with her as she grows older. moneto wrote the English lyrics and composed the song with featured singer MRCH. The live clip here comes from MRCH’s own channel.
items.altText: indiek listening notes: moneto — She (Feat. MRCH). Typographic card.

items.title: MRCH — Surrender
items.description: An alarm clock, afternoon dessert and a phone before bed become everyday opponents in “Surrender”. MRCH’s song from Oh, Life lets go of the wish to be invincible. This live clip was shared on her own channel before the EP’s release.
items.altText: indiek listening notes: MRCH — Surrender. Typographic card.

items.title: Say Sue Me — Old Town
items.description: In “Old Town”, friends have moved away while the speaker remains. Wanting to leave and wanting to stay keep trading places.
items.altText: indiek listening notes: Say Sue Me — Old Town. Typographic card.

items.title: Silica Gel — NO PAIN
items.description: “NO PAIN” invites people who have felt excluded into a house where everyone can sing together. The speaker also considers leaving and asks not to be hated, keeping that welcome unsettled.
items.altText: indiek listening notes: Silica Gel — NO PAIN. Typographic card.

items.title: Meaningful Stone — Beep-Boop, Beep-Boop
items.description: A falling construction crane makes the possibility of sudden death concrete in “Beep-Boop, Beep-Boop”. The speaker asks why attention should arrive only after someone disappears.
items.altText: indiek listening notes: Meaningful Stone — Beep-Boop, Beep-Boop. Typographic card.

items.title: Lang Lee — There is A Wolf
items.description: People seeking food are called witches, rioters and wolves in “There is A Wolf” (늑대가 나타났다). The lyric gives those accused a reply: they are the workers who make the food others enjoy.
items.altText: indiek listening notes: Lang Lee — There is A Wolf. Typographic card.

items.title: JEONGMILLA — Departing from Seoul Station
items.description: A conversation with her mother turns Seoul Station into a way of looking back at the speaker’s life: arriving for a university entrance exam, expecting to become a painter and finding a living in music. JEONGMILLA wrote the words and music.
items.altText: indiek listening notes: JEONGMILLA — Departing from Seoul Station. Typographic card.

items.title: Yoon Mirae — Breath
items.description: In “Breath”, guitar leaves plenty of space around Yoon Mirae’s voice. The song is about the ordinary things that remind you of someone after a breakup.
items.altText: indiek listening notes: Yoon Mirae — Breath. Typographic card.
